gaps.old_draft_snippet: Two-dimensional photonic crystal diffractive optical neural networks (PhC-DONNs) realize on-chip optical parallel classification schemes with multi-wavelength parallel processing capabilities [[claim:S05-P004]].
gaps.scientific_content: The specific implementation of two-dimensional photonic crystal diffractive optical neural networks (PhC-DONNs) for on-chip, multi-wavelength parallel classification is missing. The new blocks discuss general integrated circuits or metasurfaces but omit this specific architecture and its capability for wavelength-diffraction joint modulation.

gaps.old_draft_snippet: Physics-informed diffractive neural networks can approximate inverse transmission matrices to enable real-time decryption of speckle ciphertexts in all-optical high-speed schemes [[claim:S05-P003]].
gaps.scientific_content: The application of physics-informed diffractive neural networks for all-optical speckle decryption (approximating inverse transmission matrices) is absent from the new chapter. This represents a distinct security/encryption application not covered by the general imaging or classification blocks.

gaps.old_draft_snippet: Multi-layer diffractive optical neural networks (D2NNs) have been demonstrated for alphabetic image recognition, leveraging parallel pixel-wise computation to achieve inference at the speed of light [[claim:S05-P105]].
gaps.scientific_content: The specific demonstration of diffractive networks for alphabetic image recognition (distinct from MNIST digits) is lost. The new blocks focus heavily on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST and general classification, omitting this specific specialized task example.

audit.notes: Identified three gaps: 1) PhC-DONN architecture for multi-wavelength on-chip processing; 2) Physics-informed speckle decryption application; 3) Alphabetic recognition as a specific classification benchmark. These represent distinct scientific claims/architectures present in the old draft that are not substantively covered in the new block summaries.
